verdict.finder_title: Prompt comparison keeps the grid's strength axis, multiplying its image count
verdict.claim: `comparePayload()` (web/analysis.js:973-990) blanks every grid axis except the `strength_axis` this commit added to `gridPayload()` (web/generation.js:258). With a refine source set, a non-empty grid Strength box makes a prompt comparison versions × strengths × Seeds images instead of versions × Seeds. This holds even when the grid section is closed, because the box is saved with the panel and survives a reload. The server accepts it (`grid._sampling_values` keeps the axis whenever `refine` is set). The comparison preview then reads, for example, "24 images · 2 variants × 4 seeds · batch 1", and the run queues three times the images the Seeds select asked for. The fix is a `strength_axis: ''` line beside `lora_scale_axis: ''` at web/analysis.js:983.
verdict.reasoning:
The comment on `comparePayload()` (web/analysis.js:965-972) says it sends the grid's own payload "with every axis emptied". CLAUDE.md says the comparison keeps "the image count versions times Seeds". The function spreads `gridPayload()` and then blanks prompt_axis, steps_axis, cfg_axis, mu_axis, lora_scale_axis (983) and seed_axis (984). It never blanks strength_axis.

This commit added `strength_axis: els.gridStrength.disabled ? '' : els.gridStrength.value.trim()` to `gridPayload()` (web/generation.js:258). `els.gridStrength.disabled` is just `!(refineSupported && !!refineSource)` (web/sizes.js:212-215), and nothing checks whether the grid section is open. So with a refine source set, whatever is in the grid Strength box goes into every comparison. That box is also saved with the panel (`PANEL_FIELDS` includes 'gridStrength', web/panel.js:21; smoke-refine.json:99-106 checks that it survives a reload), so an old sweep left in a closed grid section is enough.

I found no guard on the server side:
- The GridRequest validators (backend/schemas.py:562-595) only refuse runs != 1, variants beside prompt_axis, and resume without a seed.
- `main` passes `strength=request.strength_axis` into `grid.axis_values` and `grid.expand` (backend/main.py:978, 991).
- `grid._sampling_values` (backend/grid.py:403-407) collapses the axis only when `request.refine is None`. Here a source is set, so it does not.
- `grid.expand` multiplies by `len(values["strength"])` (grid.py:679) and loops over it (grid.py:711).

The page does not catch it either. `previewComparison` (analysis.js:1022-1023) prints `p.images` next to its own "variants × seeds" text, giving the self-contradictory "24 images · 2 variants × 4 seeds · batch 1". `runComparison` (analysis.js:1038) posts the same payload to /api/grid. `git show 212f41c --stat` confirms the commit did not touch web/analysis.js, and no smoke runs a comparison while a refine source is set.

confirmed.title: A refine grid is refused over the base steps/strength pair that an axis replaces in every cell
confirmed.description: `_refine_leaves_a_step` is a model validator on `GenerateRequest`, so it also runs on the `GridRequest` body and on the CLI's base request (generate.py:518) before the axes apply. When a strength or steps axis is set, the base values are only fallbacks that `grid.expand` replaces in every cell, and `expand` already checks each cell by name. That per-cell check is the contract the design notes and the validator's own comment state ("for a grid is every cell ... refused here, by name, when the grid is built"). An absent strength is filled in from the profile before the check (0.1 on FLUX.1), so the refusal can name a value the user never typed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: FLUX.1 Krea dev, Steps 8, Strength box untouched, a refine source, Strength axis `0.3,0.5` (cells at 2.4 and 4 steps). /api/grid and /api/grid/preview answer 422 "strength 0.1 of 8 steps is less than one step"; `generate "a fox" --refine 1 --steps 8 --grid-strength 0.3,0.5 --dry-run` exits 2 with the same message. Steps 4 with a steps axis `20,28` is refused the same way. The workaround is to raise the unused base value.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Skip the base check on a `GridRequest` whose `strength_axis` or `steps_axis` is set (the cells are checked in `expand`), and build the CLI's base request the same way. Alternatively, move the check out of the schema into the per-cell build altogether, which also settles F3.
confirmed.evidence: `GridRequest` construction, TestClient on /api/grid/preview and the CLI dry run all refuse; with a base strength of 0.3 the same grids expand into valid cells. Re-run by hand after the workflow: refused for Steps 8 with the axis `0.3,0.5`, with and without an explicit 0.1, and for Steps 4 with a steps axis `20,28`; accepted with a base strength of 0.5.

verdict.finder_title: A grid is refused for a base strength or step count that no cell uses
verdict.claim: `GridRequest` inherits `GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step`, so the one-step refusal also runs on the grid body's base steps/strength. When a strength or steps axis is set, those values are only fallbacks that `grid.expand` replaces in every cell. A refine sweep whose every cell leaves at least one step is therefore refused with a 422 from /api/grid and /api/grid/preview, and exit 2 from the CLI, naming a steps/strength pair that no cell renders. Example on FLUX.1 Krea dev: Steps 8, Strength box 0.1 or empty (filled with the profile's 0.1), and strength axis 0.3,0.5. The design notes put the check on each cell. The workaround is to raise the unused base value.
verdict.reasoning:
`GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step` (schemas.py:119-131) is a model validator, so `GridRequest(GenerateRequest)` at schemas.py:512 inherits it. It runs on the grid body's base `steps`/`strength` once `_profile_defaults` (schemas.py:102-117) has filled a missing strength with `default_strength()`, which is 0.1 on FLUX.1 Krea dev. The `GridRequest` docstring (schemas.py:515-517) says the inherited fields are only the base that a blank axis falls back to. When `strength_axis`/`steps_axis` is set, `grid.expand` (grid.py:711-727) builds each cell as a new `GenerateRequest` with `steps=step_count` and `strength=amount`. That re-runs the same validator once per cell, which is the per-cell refusal the design notes describe ("which for a grid is every cell, at submit, by name", design-notes.md around line 479).

Nothing upstream stops the base from being checked as well. FastAPI validates the `GridRequest` body before `main._expand` (main.py:950) or `preview_grid` runs, so the base pair is refused even though no cell renders it. The page sends the base through `gridPayload()` (web/generation.js:249-263, which spreads `collect()`). `collect()` sends `strength: num(els.strength)` while the box is enabled (generation.js:36), and the server fills an empty box with 0.1, so the box cannot be left blank to avoid the check. The CLI does the same: it builds the base `GenerateRequest` with `steps=args.steps` and `strength=args.strength` (None, so filled with 0.1) at generate.py:518-540, before calling `grid.expand` at line 590, and exits 2 there.

The test that looks like it covers this, test_api_refine.py:110-126, sets the base `"strength": 0.5` so the refusal comes from a cell. No test checks that a grid whose base fails but whose cells all pass is accepted. Nothing in CLAUDE.md or the design notes says the base should be checked when an axis replaces it.

Impact: a valid sweep is refused with a message naming a steps/strength pair that no cell uses. The workaround is to raise the unused box value. No data or reproduction keys are affected, so severity is low.

verdict.finder_title: Base (steps, strength) pair is validated even when an axis replaces it
verdict.claim: `_refine_leaves_a_step` (schemas.py:126) is inherited by `GridRequest` and also runs on the CLI's base `GenerateRequest` (generate.py:518). It checks the base (steps, strength) pair, with an absent strength filled from the profile (0.1 on FLUX.1 dev), even when `--grid-strength`/`strength_axis` or `--grid-steps`/`steps_axis` replaces that value in every cell. A grid whose cells all leave at least one step is then refused, with an error naming a pair no cell would run, on both the CLI (exit 2) and `/api/grid` and `/api/grid/preview` (422). The documented contract is a per-cell refusal. `grid.expand` already checks each cell.
verdict.reasoning:
`GenerateRequest._profile_defaults` (schemas.py:115-116) fills an absent strength from `default_strength()`, which is 0.1 on FLUX.1 Krea dev. `_refine_leaves_a_step` (schemas.py:119-130) then checks that base (steps, strength) pair whenever `refine` is set. `GridRequest` (schemas.py:512) inherits both validators unchanged, and the CLI builds its base as a plain `GenerateRequest` at generate.py:518-536, with `strength=args.strength`. That base check runs before `grid.expand` (generate.py:590). Inside `expand`, the axis values replace the base steps or strength: `_sampling_values` at grid.py:390 and 403-406, then the per-cell `GenerateRequest(**{..., "steps": step_count, "strength": amount})` at grid.py:711-726. Each cell is checked there again.

The design notes (design-notes.md, refine section, around line 98-100) state the contract: the refusal applies "when the request is built - which for a grid is every cell, at submit". CLAUDE.md says the same: "refused when the request is built, so per grid cell". The validator's own comment also describes a per-cell refusal.

When an axis replaces the base value, the base pair is not a cell, yet it is refused. The resulting message names a pair that no cell would run. No guard upstream exempts the base when an axis is set. The existing tests avoid the case. test_api_refine.py:110-121 passes `strength: 0.5` as its base. test_refine.py:259-274 uses steps=10 and builds the base without the validator path at issue. test_cli.py:585 tests only a plain request. This does not appear to be a deliberate choice: nothing in the docs justifies checking a base that an axis replaces.

Severity is low. The workaround is easy: pass a `--strength`/`--steps` that satisfies the base. The case also needs low base steps. On the page, the Steps box defaults to the profile's 28, and 28 x 0.1 = 2.8 leaves steps. A CLI user who lowers `--steps` for a fast strength sweep and omits `--strength` hits it naturally.
verdict.reproduction:

- `GridRequest(prompt='x', refine=1, steps=4, steps_axis='20,28')` raised "strength 0.1 of 4 steps is less than one step".

- Control: adding `--strength 0.3` to the first command passed request construction and `expand`. It stopped only at the later gallery check, "no gallery database ... so there is no image 1 to refine". That shows the base pair is the only cause.

verdict.finder_title: Strength axis refused over the panel's strength, which no cell uses
verdict.claim: GridRequest inherits GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step (schemas.py:119-130), so a refine grid is refused when its base steps × strength leaves no step, even when a steps or strength axis replaces those base values and every cell grid.expand builds is valid. Example: FLUX.1 Krea dev, Steps 8, Strength at its seeded 0.1, strength axis 0.2,0.3,0.4 gets a 422 "strength 0.1 of 8 steps is less than one step". The per-cell check in expand already refuses any bad cell by name, which is the documented contract ("for a grid is every cell"). The CLI does the same at generate.py:517-535, where it builds the base GenerateRequest before the --grid-steps/--grid-strength axes apply. Impact is a spurious, clearly worded refusal that raising the panel's Steps or Strength works around; severity low.
verdict.reasoning:
`GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step` (schemas.py:119-130) is a model_validator, so `GridRequest(GenerateRequest)` (schemas.py:512) inherits it. It runs on the grid's base `steps`/`strength` after `_profile_defaults` (schemas.py:102-117) has filled the strength from the profile (0.1 on FLUX.1 Krea dev, model_defaults.py:276). FastAPI parses the body of `/api/grid` and `/api/grid/preview` straight into GridRequest (main.py:1022, main.py:1149), so the check runs before any route code. Nothing upstream guards it. The page's `gridPayload()` (web/generation.js:250) spreads `collect()`, which sends the Strength box. That box is seeded with the profile's 0.1 (status.js:22), and the page runs no step check of its own.

When an axis is set, the base value is never a cell. `grid._sampling_values` uses `parse_axis(strength) or [request.strength]` (grid.py:403-406), and the steps axis works the same way. `grid.expand` then rebuilds every cell as its own `GenerateRequest` with the axis values (grid.py:711-727). That runs the same validator per cell and refuses a bad one by name. `test_refine.py:273` and `test_api_refine.py:110-121` both cover that path. So for a grid, the base check can only add one thing: refusing a grid in which every cell is valid.

The contract puts the refusal on the cells. Design notes, "The refine pass": "refuses `int(steps * strength) < 1` when the request is built - which for a grid is every cell". CLAUDE.md: "refused when the request is built, so per grid cell". The validator's own comment says the same. No test chose the base-refusal behaviour on purpose: the only grid refusal test (test_api_refine.py:113) uses a valid base strength of 0.5. The CLI has the same spurious refusal. generate.py:517-535 builds the base `GenerateRequest` from `--steps`/`--strength` with `refine=` set before the grid axes are applied, so `--steps 8 --refine N --grid-strength 0.2,0.4` on Krea dev is refused at strength 0.1.

Severity: low rather than medium. It only fires when the panel's base steps × strength is below one step and an axis replaces it. The refusal is a clear 422 naming the base values, nothing runs wrongly, and raising the panel's Steps or Strength works around it. Still, it refuses work the contract allows, and its message names a value no cell uses.

verdict.finder_title: With no refine pass, the step-count error pre-empts the no-pass refusal
verdict.claim: `GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step` (backend/schemas.py:126) refuses a low strength while the body is validated, without checking whether the running checkpoint has a refine pass. `/api/generate` and `/api/grid` both validate the body before `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:391-409) runs. So on a low-step checkpoint with no pass (klein 4 steps, Anima/ERNIE Turbo 8), an API request with `refine` and a low explicit strength gets "strength X of N steps is less than one step; raise the strength or the steps" instead of "has no refine pass". Following that advice only produces a second, different 422. The CLI (generate.py:474-487) deliberately checks for a missing pass first for exactly this reason. Both paths still refuse and nothing runs; only the reason is wrong. The page cannot send this request.
verdict.reasoning:
This is real but minor. A request for a pass the checkpoint cannot run is refused either way. Only the reason given is wrong.

Path traced:
- backend/schemas.py:119-131: `GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step` is a `model_validator(mode="after")`. It runs whenever `refine` is set and refuses `int(steps*strength) < 1`. It does not ask whether the checkpoint has a refine pass.
- `GridRequest` (schemas.py:512) and `PromptAnalysisRequest` inherit this validator.
- main.py:936-942: the `/api/generate` route takes `request: GenerateRequest`. FastAPI validates the body before the handler runs, so `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:391-409), which raises "has no refine pass", is never reached.
- `/api/grid` goes through `_expand`, which calls `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:967). Its `GridRequest` body is validated first in the same way.
- `applied()` (schemas.py:243-248) would drop `refine` on such a checkpoint anyway, so the step bound concerns a pass that can never run.

The CLI orders the two checks the other way on purpose. The comment at generate.py:474-477 reads "a strength that also happens to leave no step of that checkpoint's few would otherwise be the error reported, about a pass that could never have run". The server does not follow that ordering. The design notes (refine section) say a request is "refused at submit (`_refuse_unusable_inputs`, and the CLI before its load) where the checkpoint has no pass". Over HTTP that refusal is pre-empted.

Nothing upstream prevents it:
- The page sends `refine` only where `refineSupported`, and the Strength box is dead otherwise. So only a direct API client can send this request.
- The profiles with no pass include several low-step ones: klein (4 steps), and Anima Turbo and ERNIE Turbo (8).
- klein's default strength (0.4 → 1 step) passes. An explicit low strength is needed to trigger it.

The existing test tests/test_api_refine.py:122-125 shows the schema-level 422 reaching the client before any route code. That test runs on the default FLUX checkpoint, where a pass exists, so it does not cover this case.

Severity is low: both paths refuse, nothing runs and no data is affected. The client is just told to raise the strength or steps, then gets a second, different refusal.

verdict.finder_title: Server reports 'less than one step' instead of 'no refine pass'
verdict.claim:
The step check runs while the request body is parsed (schemas.py:119-131; `GridRequest` inherits it), before `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:402-410) ever runs. So on a checkpoint with no refine pass, a `/api/generate`, `/api/grid` or `/api/grid/preview` request whose explicit *base* strength or steps leave less than one step gets a 422 value_error. It says "strength X of N steps is less than one step; raise the strength or the steps", which can never fix the request. Only after raising the strength does the client get the real cause, "has no refine pass".

This reverses the order the CLI chooses on purpose and justifies at generate.py:477-488. A low value on `strength_axis` is not affected, because `grid.expand` runs after the capability check.

It is reachable only through direct API calls with explicit low values. The page never sends a source where `refineSupported` is false, and every profile's default strength leaves a step. No request is wrongly accepted.
verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed. The server reports the wrong refusal first, but only to direct API clients that send an explicit low strength or step count.

How the ordering happens:
- `GenerateRequest._refine_leaves_a_step` (schemas.py:119-131) is a pydantic `model_validator`. It runs while FastAPI parses the body, before the handler at main.py:937 is entered.
- It checks only `self.refine is not None`, not whether the checkpoint has a pass.
- The capability refusal is `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:391-410). `generate()` reaches it at main.py:942, so for `/api/generate` the step check always wins.
- `GridRequest` subclasses `GenerateRequest` (schemas.py:512), so a grid's or preview's *base* strength is checked at parse time too.
- A low value on `strength_axis` is checked later, in `grid.expand` inside `_expand`. That runs after `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:967), so the grid's axis path gets the right order.
- The CLI orders these checks on purpose (generate.py:477-488). Its comment names this exact case as the one to avoid: "a strength that also happens to leave no step ... would otherwise be the error reported, about a pass that could never have run".
- The CLI test calls its no-pass refusal "the same refusal the server makes at submit" (test_cli.py:586-590). For this input it is not the same.
- The first message advises "raise the strength or the steps", which can never make the request succeed.

What limits the reach:
- The page never sends `refine` where `refineSupported` is false: `collect()` sends the source only where supported, per CLAUDE.md, and smoke-conditioning.json:29 asserts `collect().refine === null`. So the UI path is guarded.
- Every catalogue profile's default strength leaves at least one step of its default steps. I computed this for all 20 `launch.CHECKPOINTS`: every row was True, e.g. klein 4 steps at 0.4 and Krea-2-Turbo 8 at 0.4. So an API request that omits `strength` gets the correct "no refine pass" message.
- The bad message needs an explicit strength or step count below one step on a checkpoint with no pass, e.g. klein or Krea 2 via the API.
- No request is wrongly accepted or run; only the message and its advice are wrong.
- CLAUDE.md and design-notes.md require both refusals at submit but do not fix their order on the server. The defect is the server and CLI disagreeing, with the server doing what the CLI's comment calls wrong.

confirmed.title: The duplicate count misses strengths that start the schedule at the same step
confirmed.description: Every sibling uses strength only to pick an integer start index (the flow pipelines `t_start = int(n - n*s)`, SDXL `n - int(n*s)`), so two strengths with the same index render byte-identical images under one seed. `cell_key` keys on the strength as typed (`refine_key` "id@0.6" against "id@0.7"), so `duplicate_count`, documented as comparing cells "as the pipeline will *run* them", reports none, and the preview's "would be identical" and the CLI's dry-run warning stay silent. Low-strength FLUX.1 sweeps, which the design notes recommend, and the few-step checkpoints hit it most. The run itself is correct: duplicates render by design, and the hash-based distinct count reports them afterwards.
confirmed.failure_scenario: FLUX.1 Krea dev at 28 steps, axis `0.05-0.15x0.01`: 11 cells, 4 distinct start indices, 0 duplicates reported. schnell (4 steps), `0.5-0.9x0.1`: 2 duplicates, 0 reported. Z-Image Turbo (8 steps), `0.2-0.5x0.05`: 4 duplicates, 0 reported. The sheet labels identical images as different strengths.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `duplicate_count` only, compare refine cells by the start index the sibling will compute (the flow or the SDXL rounding, by the checkpoint's family) rather than the raw strength. Keep `CellKey` and `run_id` on the raw strength.

verdict.finder_title: duplicate_count misses refine strengths that start at the same step
verdict.claim:
`grid.duplicate_count` (backend/grid.py:505) compares refine cells by their raw strength through `cell_key`/`refine_key` (grid.py:122-129, 500). The image-to-image pipelines use strength only to choose the schedule's start index: flow pipelines take `t_start = int(steps - steps*strength)`, SDXL takes `steps - int(steps*strength)`.

So strengths that land on the same index render byte-identical images, yet the preview and the CLI report 0 duplicates. Example: on FLUX.1 Krea dev at 28 steps, the axis 0.05-0.15x0.01 is 11 cells but only 4 distinct images, and 7 duplicates go unreported. On SDXL at 28 steps, 0.40 and 0.41 both start at index 17. The sheet then labels identical cells as different strengths.
verdict.reasoning:
I found nothing upstream that stops this. The chain:

1. **The sibling pipelines only use strength to pick a start index.** In the installed diffusers 0.40:
   - `FluxImg2ImgPipeline` uses `strength` in three places: `check_inputs` (the [0,1] range check), `get_timesteps` at pipeline_flux_img2img.py:477-486, and the error message at :917-921. `get_timesteps` computes `t_start = int(max(steps - steps*strength, 0))`. The noise level then comes from `latent_timestep = timesteps[:1]` (:923) and goes into `prepare_latents`/`scale_noise` (:656).
   - SDXL img2img (pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py:647-657) uses `int(steps*strength)`, and `denoising_start` is never passed.
   - Z-Image (:285) and Qwen-Image (:256) img2img use the same flow `get_timesteps`.
   - So two strengths with the same `t_start` give the pipeline identical inputs.

2. **The backend passes strength straight through.** `DiffusersBackend.generate` hands `request.strength` to the pipeline unchanged (diffusers_backend.py:643-647). Strength also drives `steps_run`, progress and the preview sigma, but none of those touch pixels.

3. **Equal inputs give equal hashes.** docs/verified.md's Refine pass section records "The same pass twice is the same hash, on all three".

4. **Nothing upstream folds strength to its start index:**
   - `GenerateRequest.applied()` (schemas.py:180-) only resets strength to the default when there is no source.
   - `grid.expand` (grid.py:711-724) builds one cell per raw value.
   - `cell_key` uses `refine_key(refine, strength)` (grid.py:122-129, 500), keyed on the strength rounded to 6 decimals.
   - So `duplicate_count` (grid.py:505-525) sees every strength as a distinct key.

5. **Both the server and the CLI rely on this count.** `/api/grid/preview` (main.py:1173) and the CLI warning (generate.py:835) both call `duplicate_count`. The page shows the warning only from `p.duplicates` (generation.js:331-335; analysis.js:1018-1025). There is no other check.

6. **This breaks the stated contract:**
   - The `duplicate_count` docstring says cells are "Compared as the pipeline will *run* them".
   - `GridPreview.duplicates` (schemas.py:637-643) promises "Cells that will render the very same image".
   - The comment in `applied()` (schemas.py:233-236) says an axis that changes no pixel should read as "the one image repeated - which is what `duplicate_count` is there to say".
   - The design notes say "A strength is an index into the checkpoint's schedule", but no rule handles duplicates on this axis.

7. **The trigger is the use the design notes recommend.** The FLUX default strength is 0.1, and "The strength axis exists to put the candidates on one sheet". A fine sweep near 0.1 is that use, and at 28 steps the granularity is 1/28 ≈ 0.036.

**One correction to the reviewer's SDXL arithmetic:** `t_start` is 17 for both 0.40 and 0.41 (28 − int(11.2) = 28 − int(11.48) = 17). The reviewer gave 11, which is the number of steps that run, not the start index. Either way the two are identical.

**Severity is low.** The duplicate cells still render correctly and are priced correctly, because duplicates are only warned about, never skipped. The harm is a missing warning, wasted GPU time, and sheet cells labelled as different strengths that show the same image.
verdict.reproduction:
I wrote scratchpad/probe_strength_dupes.py and ran it with `uv run python`. The model was the default FLUX.1-Krea-dev; the request was 28 steps, 1536x1536, refine=1, seed 5, strength axis "0.05-0.15x0.01".

The probe printed:

- Flux `t_start` per strength: [(0.05,26),(0.06,26),(0.07,26),(0.08,25),(0.09,25),(0.1,25),(0.11,24),(0.12,24),(0.13,24),(0.14,24),(0.15,23)]
- `distinct flux starts 4`
- `sdxl 0.40/0.41 17 17`
- `applied()` leaves every strength unchanged: [0.05 ... 0.15]

I did not run anything on the GPU. Byte-identical output for equal `t_start` follows from the diffusers source, which uses strength only through `int()`, plus the determinism verified.md records.

verdict.finder_title: Strength sweep duplicates (same start step) are not counted
verdict.claim: grid.duplicate_count builds cell keys from the strength as typed (refine_key 'id@0.6' vs 'id@0.7'). The sibling pipelines turn strength into an integer start index (flow pipelines: t_start = int(n - n*s); SDXL: t_start = n - int(n*s)), so different strengths with the same start index make byte-identical images under one seed. The grid preview's "N would be identical to another cell" and the CLI's dry-run WARNING miss them. Example: schnell, 4 steps, strength axis 0.5-0.9x0.1, has 2 real duplicates and reports 0. Z-Image Turbo, 8 steps, 0.2-0.5x0.05, has 4 and reports 0. This contradicts duplicate_count's own docstring and main.py:953. The run itself is correct: duplicates are rendered by design, so the estimate is right, and the hash-based distinct count reports the repeats afterwards. The gap is only in the advisory before the run, and it shows up mainly on few-step checkpoints.
verdict.reasoning:
I couldn't refute this. In every sibling pipeline the strength does one thing: it picks the start index. diffusers flux/pipeline_flux_img2img.py:477-486 (copied into z_image img2img:285 and qwenimage img2img:256) sets t_start = int(n - n*s). SDXL img2img:647-657 sets init = int(n*s), t_start = n - init. After that, `timesteps[:1]` sets the noise level in prepare_latents, and apart from check_inputs no other line reads strength. The app's _refine adds nothing that depends on strength either: diffusers_backend.py:647 only passes kwargs["strength"].

So two strengths that give the same t_start, under one seed, make the same latents and the same denoise. verified.md:332 records that the same pass run twice gives the same hash on all three pipelines, so those cells are byte-identical.

No guard upstream catches this. GenerateRequest.applied() (schemas.py:244-249) normalises strength only when there is no source. _refine_leaves_a_step only refuses fewer than one step. duplicate_count (grid.py:505-525) compares cell_key, and cell_key carries refine_key(request.refine, request.strength) = "id@0.6" vs "id@0.7" (grid.py:129, 500). So the key is the strength as typed, not as run. Both the server preview (main.py:1173) and the CLI warning (generate.py:835-838) use that count.

This contradicts what the code says about itself: duplicate_count's docstring ("How many cells would render the very same image... Compared as the pipeline will *run* them, not as the panel spelled them"), main.py:953 ("counts the cells that would render an identical image"), and the lora_scale comment in schemas.py:233-236 ("look like a sweep instead of the one image repeated - which is what duplicate_count is there to say").

Two corrections to the reviewer:
- The estimate and image count including the copies is not itself wrong. By design, duplicates are still rendered (design-notes "Content hashes and duplicate counts"), so those cells really do run. After the run, the hash-based distinct count does say "only N distinct".
- The miss is in the advisory before the run: the preview's "would be identical to another cell" and the CLI's WARNING.

Context that lowers the stakes: this is advisory only, and it needs a sweep finer than 1/steps, which is natural only on few-step checkpoints (schnell with 4 steps, Z-Image Turbo with 8). The count was never a full pixel-identity check: an SDXL CFG axis of 0.5,0.8 below the 1.0 threshold also renders identical images and also counts 0, and I reproduced that. The design notes describe the count as "applied key repeats", which the code does implement.
verdict.reproduction:
Scratch scripts are under the scratchpad (verify_strength_dupes.py, verify_strength_dupes2.py) and were run with `uv run python`.

(1) With LOCAL_DIFFUSION_MODEL_ID=FLUX.1-schnell (profile: steps 4, refine_strength 0.5, refine_supported True), I ran expand(GenerateRequest(steps=4, refine=7, strength=0.5), strength='0.5-0.9x0.1'). It gave 5 cells keyed 7@0.5, 7@0.6, 7@0.7, 7@0.8, 7@0.9. The flow pipeline's own formula gives steps run of 2, 3, 3, 4, 4. duplicate_count with applied(refine_supported=True) printed 0.

(2) With Z-Image-Turbo (steps 8, refine_strength 0.25), strength '0.2-0.5x0.05' gave start indices [6, 6, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4]: 4 true duplicates, yet duplicate_count printed 0.

(3) For the pre-existing analogue, an SDXL-style CFG axis '0.5,0.8' with threshold 1.0 also gave duplicate_count 0.

confirmed.title: An off-catalogue checkpoint's refine request is accepted on the profile's guess, then rendered without the pass
confirmed.description: Before a load, the submit refusal reads the profile's `refine_supported`, which is a family-token guess. For repo ids outside the catalogue that carry `flux` (FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, FLUX.1-Fill-dev, FLUX.2-dev) or `qwen-image` (Qwen-Image-Edit, -Edit-2509), the guess is True, but in diffusers 0.40 their classes have no image-to-image sibling. Nothing checks again after `ensure_loaded`. `generate()`'s `applied()` then drops the source and resets the strength without a log line, and the job ends "done". The rows are honest (refine None), but a strength sweep becomes N identical text-to-image renders: the "night of new pictures" the design notes give as the reason for the refusal. On the server this affects jobs submitted before the first load; on the CLI it affects every run. **The verifiers split on this one.** F5's verifier confirmed the server's half, since the refusal exists to prevent exactly this outcome. A separate candidate for the CLI's half of the same path (generate.py:927) was refuted by its verifier as the documented structure: "refused at submit ... where the checkpoint has no pass ... and dropped by `applied()` where it gets past that" (design-notes.md:495-503), with a check after the load called reasonable hardening rather than a fix. Both agree on the mechanics and that it needs an id outside the catalogue. Read F5 as a gap in the design, not code departing from its notes.

Optionally tighten the guesses for the known ids without a sibling.

verdict.finder_title: Refine accepted on the profile's guess, then silently dropped after the load
verdict.claim: For repo ids outside the catalogue whose id contains a family token (`flux` for FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, FLUX.1-Fill-dev and FLUX.2-dev; `qwen-image` for Qwen-Image-Edit and -Edit-2509), the profile guesses `refine_supported` True, but in diffusers 0.40 their classes have no image-to-image sibling. The server's submit refusal (main.py:402-410, which reads `_merged_defaults` of an unloaded `describe()`) and the CLI's check (generate.py:481) both use that guess before the load. Nothing checks again after `ensure_loaded`/`load()`. `generate()` at diffusers_backend.py:541 then drops the source and resets the strength through `applied()`, with no log line, and the job finishes "done" with plain text-to-image renders: a strength sweep gives identical images. The saved row stays honest (refine None). On the server this affects only jobs submitted before the first load; on the CLI it affects every run. It needs an off-catalogue id, hence low severity.
verdict.reasoning:
I traced the path end to end and found no guard on it. The one condition is a repo id outside the catalogue that still matches a family token.

1. **The guess decides at submit.** `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:402-410) reads `_merged_defaults(backend.describe())["refine_supported"]`. While `_pipe` is None, `describe()` returns `refine_supported: None` (diffusers_backend.py:798). `_merged_defaults` (main.py:298-308) then keeps the profile's value.
2. **The guess is wrong for these ids.** `_PROFILES` matches on the first token. `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Kontext-dev`, `FLUX.1-Fill-dev` and `FLUX.2-dev` all hit `flux` (model_defaults.py:262-276: `refine_supported` True, strength 0.1). `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit` and `-Edit-2509` hit `qwen-image` (around line 428: True, 0.3). In diffusers 0.40, `refine.sibling()` returns None for every one of their classes. Each class still has `generator` and `callback_on_step_end`, so `load()`'s `_REQUIRED_PARAMS` check (diffusers_backend.py:176-183) lets it through.
3. **Nothing checks again after the load.** `jobs._run` awaits `ensure_loaded` (jobs.py:380) and goes straight to the cells. jobs.py never mentions refine apart from a comment at line 499.
4. **`generate()` drops the source without a word.** Line 541 calls `self.applied(request)`, which now uses the live `_refine_supported()` (False, lines 314-321). `schemas.applied` (schemas.py:244-249) sets `refine` to None and puts `strength` back to `default_strength()`. Line 540 logs a dropped negative prompt; nothing logs a dropped source.
5. **The CLI has the same gap.** `generate.py:481` checks only the profile, and it always runs before `backend.load()` (line 927). Nothing checks again after that.

**Why this is a defect and not the documented fallback.** The design notes say the submit refusal is there to stop "a night of refinements that rendered as plain text-to-image at the larger size". CLAUDE.md says an unsupported checkpoint "is refused at submit and by the CLI". `applied()` dropping the source "where it gets past that" is documented as the record-keeping fallback, not the guard. The README invites pasting an unlisted repo id. The fallback profile already refuses to promise a pass for unrecognised ids (test_refine.py:70-71, "not promised one either, until it loads"). Ids caught by a family token get no such caution: `test_the_profile_guess_matches_the_installed_diffusers` only covers the catalogue's `CASES`.

**Why low and not medium.**
- It needs an off-catalogue id.
- On the server it only affects jobs submitted before the first load. After that, `describe()` returns the live False and both the refusal and the page's greying work.
- The saved row and PNG are honest (refine None).
- Of the five ids, Kontext and FLUX.2-dev run text-to-image cleanly with `image=None`. Fill and the Qwen edit pipelines probably fail for other reasons. The real cost is wasted renders, not corrupt data.

**Anchor.** The reviewer put this at diffusers_backend.py:541. That line is where the source disappears. The guard that fails to fire is main.py:404, and the wrong guess comes from the family profiles (model_defaults.py:272, and the `qwen-image` entry).
verdict.reproduction:
I wrote scratchpad/verify_guess_vs_live.py and ran it with `uv run python` (backend.config imported first). For each of the five ids it printed `guess True`, strength 0.1 (FLUX) or 0.3 (Qwen), `sibling None`, `gen True`, `cb True`, and `image` optional (default None). FluxPipeline printed its FluxImg2ImgPipeline sibling, as a control.

I wrote scratchpad/verify_kontext_drop.py and ran it with LOCAL_DIFFUSION_MODEL_ID=black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Kontext-dev, using the real DiffusersBackend and a `FluxKontextPipeline` instance made with `object.__new__` plus its real call signature. Output:
- describe refine_supported unloaded: None
- merged (what `_refuse_unusable_inputs` reads): True
- applied unloaded: 7 0.3
- `_refine_supported` loaded: False
- applied loaded: None 0.1

So submit accepts the request, and after the load `applied()` (the call `generate()` makes at line 541) drops the source and resets the strength to 0.1. I did not run the HTTP route myself. The reviewer's scratch API test covers that part, and every piece of it matches the code above. `git status` is still clean.

verdict.finder_title: Status gives refine_strength null for a live pass, so the Strength box goes stale
verdict.claim: `_merged_defaults` (backend/main.py:298-310) swaps in the live `refine_supported` but leaves the profile's `refine_strength` at None. So for a checkpoint off the profile table whose loaded pipeline has an img2img sibling, /api/status reports `refine_supported` true and `refine_strength` null. Meanwhile `schemas.default_strength()` and the Refine tooltip both use 0.4. `applyDefaults` (web/status.js:22) only seeds the Strength box from a number. A page kept open while the server restarts from a profiled checkpoint (e.g. FLUX.1 Krea dev, 0.1) onto such a checkpoint therefore keeps the old checkpoint's untouched strength, and sends it with every refine. The tooltip still says 0.4, while Steps, CFG and Mu re-seed. A fresh page load or Reset shows 0.4, so the stale value only survives across a server restart.
verdict.reasoning:
The trace holds end to end.

Server side: `_merged_defaults` (backend/main.py:298-310) starts from `defaults_for(model_id)`. For an id the table does not know, that is `_FALLBACK` (model_defaults.py:768-795), which has `refine_supported: False, refine_strength: None`. The function then replaces `refine_supported` with the live answer, but nothing ever fills in `refine_strength`. The server's own default goes the other way:
- `schemas.default_strength()` (schemas.py:30) gives `DEFAULT_STRENGTH` = 0.4 for that id.
- `hints_for` (model_defaults.py:947) does the same, so the tooltip says "starts at 0.4 on this checkpoint". It handles this exact case on purpose, per the comment at 944-946.

So /api/status publishes `refine_supported: True` beside `refine_strength: null`. That contradicts status.js:19-21 ("Null where the checkpoint has no pass; the box is dead there") and the CLAUDE.md contract that the default (`refine.DEFAULT_STRENGTH` where the profile names none) is "seeded into the Strength box per control". `ModelStatus.defaults` (schemas.py:892) is a plain dict and changes nothing on the way out.

Page side: `applyDefaults` (status.js:22) writes the box only when `refine_strength` is a number. Every other write to the box:
- gallery.js:380: Reuse of a refined record.
- panel.js:113: Reset, which would give 0.4 via `?? REFINE_STRENGTH`.
- `restoreSampling` (panel.js:136-146): runs once, and only for a matching model.

`refreshStatus` deliberately supports a server restarted under another checkpoint while the page stays open (status.js:127-139). In that case Steps, CFG and Mu re-seed to the new profile, but Strength keeps the old one's value. `refineFrom` (gallery.js:439-441) quotes `els.strength.value`. `collect()` (generation.js:36) sends it once a source enables the box (sizes.js:213-214). `leaves_a_step(28, 0.1)` passes, so nothing refuses it. SDXL img2img's `get_timesteps` (diffusers pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py:650) then runs int(28*0.1) = 2 steps, where 0.4 would run 11.

No guard exists upstream. Any id is accepted through `--model`, `LOCAL_DIFFUSION_MODEL_ID` or the menu (`launch.py:432`, `repos.get(answer, answer)`). `refine.sibling(StableDiffusionXLPipeline)` resolves to `StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline`.

verdict.finder_title: Plain reindex copies a refine id verbatim, so it can name an unrelated image
verdict.claim:
A PNG-only `reindex` stores the PNG chunk's `refine` id as it is (storage.py:892). On `--from` it also leaves that id unchanged in the copied PNG (reindex.py:395). A gallery id only means something in the database that wrote the file. So after `reindex --from <other gallery>` without `--database`, or an in-place rebuild after the database is lost (AUTOINCREMENT ids renumber when earlier rows were deleted), a refined row can name an unrelated image or itself.

The refusals at main.py:402-412 and generate.py:633-642 only check that the id exists. Re-render (main.py:1106), Reuse (gallery.js:377) and `--from-image` (generate.py:319) therefore run a refine pass of the wrong picture and record it as the reproduction.

This is the same verbatim read reference ids already had before the commit, and the commit mirrors it on purpose (test_refine.py:375-378). So it is an inherited flaw extended to the new field, limited to recovery and merge paths.
verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds, and I reproduced both scenarios.

How the bad id gets in:
- In the PNG-only reindex path, `reindex.reindex` (reindex.py:369-405) sends each file's chunk to `storage.index_file`. `index_file` stores `"refine": meta.get("refine")` as it is (storage.py:892-893), with no remap or check.
- On `--from`, `_copy_in(path, target, meta)` (reindex.py:395) writes the same id back into the copied PNG unchanged. So `--from-image` on the copied file reads the foreign id too (generate.py:319-320).

How it is used afterwards, with no guard on the way:
- Re-render builds the request with `refine=r.refine` (main.py:1106).
- Reuse sets `refineSource = {id: rec.refine}` (web/gallery.js:377).
- `--from-image` copies `meta["refine"]` (generate.py:319-320). Its comment says "the id is this gallery's own, like a reference", which is exactly the assumption that breaks here.
- The only refusals are `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:402-412) and generate.py:633-642. Both call `storage.reference_paths([refine])`, which checks only that some row with that id and its file exist. Nothing checks that it is the same picture (no hash, no filename).
- The lightbox shows "refine of N" (web/lightbox.js) without validating it.

So a wrong id passes every check, and a refine of the wrong image is rendered and recorded as the original's reproduction.

Only the database merge remaps the id (reindex.py:295-304). Design-notes 1092-1101 give the reason: "rather than left pointing at an unrelated destination row". The PNG-only path has no such handling.

Why this is real but low severity:
- The commit chose this on purpose. The test at tests/test_refine.py:375-378 says so ("as a reference's ids are read back: the id is the one the gallery that wrote the file knew the source by"), and design-notes 497 says "Everything else is the reference image's design".
- Reference ids have had the same verbatim read in `index_file` since before this commit. The README paragraph (1482-1490) was not changed by the commit.
- Neither the design notes nor CLAUDE.md justify keeping ids verbatim on the PNG-only path as safe, and the code's own premise (generate.py:316-318) is broken by it. So it is a defect, but one the commit inherited and extended to a new field rather than introduced.
- It happens only on recovery or merge paths: a database lost and then rebuilt in place (where earlier deletions, common with Delete unstarred, shift every id), or a foreign gallery copied in without its `--database`.

It divides a refine row's `duration_ms` by `refine.steps_run`, which is `max(1, int(steps*strength))` (refine.py:142), and a direct row's by `steps`. It returns the median.
- **What a refine row's `duration_ms` covers:** it is `elapsed_ms // len(images)` (jobs.py:584). That time is per image and includes the source load and Lanczos resize (`refine.source_image`, diffusers_backend.py:646). `_refine` (diffusers_backend.py:719-731) also makes one sibling call per image, so the text encode, VAE encode and VAE decode are paid per image as well.
- **The flow pipelines' count:** in the installed diffusers, `FluxImg2ImgPipeline.get_timesteps` (pipeline_flux_img2img.py:477-486) runs `steps - int(steps - steps*strength)`. At 28 steps and 0.1 that is 3 steps, while `steps_run` counts 2. SDXL's img2img (pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py:650) floors, so it matches `steps_run`.
- **The estimate:** `grid.estimate_seconds` multiplies by `denoised_steps`, which is `steps_run` for a refine cell and `steps` for a direct one (grid.py:560-594).

verdict.finder_title: Under model offload the VAE stays on the card through a pass's whole denoise
verdict.claim: Under offload=model, each refine call encodes the source with the shared, hooked VAE before denoising. The VAE is last in the loaded pipeline's offload chain, so no hook moves it off the card until `_refine`'s final `maybe_free_model_hooks()`. The VAE (about 0.16 GiB in 16-bit) therefore stays resident beside the denoiser for the whole pass, which does not happen in a text-to-image call. This matches the 0.16 GiB higher refine peaks the commit itself measured (docs/verified.md:316, 318). README.md:600-601, docs/design-notes.md:398 and the commit message say nothing more is held on the card. That is accurate only in the sense that no weights are duplicated; a pass's peak card use is slightly higher than a direct render at the same size. It is stock diffusers behaviour and costs little, so the defect is mainly the documentation's overstatement, or a missing VAE offload after the encode.
verdict.reasoning:
The offload hooks belong to the loaded pipeline. `loading.place_pipeline` (backend/backends/loading.py:292-293) calls `enable_model_cpu_offload` on it, so the chain follows the loaded class's `model_cpu_offload_seq`: FluxPipeline "text_encoder->text_encoder_2->image_encoder->transformer->vae" (pipeline_flux.py:179), SDXL "...->unet->vae" (pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl.py:223), Z-Image "text_encoder->transformer->vae" (pipeline_z_image.py:142). The sibling shares those hooked modules (`refine.build`).

In accelerate's `CpuOffload.pre_forward` (accelerate/hooks.py:748-756), each module offloads only its *previous* hook's module before moving itself onto the card. The VAE comes last, so it is the previous module of nothing. The only thing that offloads it is `maybe_free_model_hooks`. `AutoencoderKL.encode`/`decode` are wrapped in `apply_forward_hook` (autoencoder_kl.py:170, 213), so encoding the source does trigger the VAE hook and moves the VAE onto the card. The image-to-image call encodes the prompt, then the source (VAE now on the card), then denoises. The transformer's hook offloads only text_encoder_2, so the VAE stays beside the denoiser for every step. In a text-to-image call the VAE first moves on at decode, after the denoise.

`_refine` (diffusers_backend.py:719-731) frees the hooks only in its `finally`, after the last image. Under offload=model (the default) a pass therefore holds the VAE's weights on the card through the denoise, which a direct render does not.

No guard upstream changes this: `applied()`, the submit refusals and the CLI only decide whether a pass runs, not where components sit. The commit's own card measurements fit it. In docs/verified.md:316 and 318, refine peak is 3.89 against 3.73 GiB direct (WAI) and 12.54 against 12.38 (FLUX at the same 1536x1536). Both deltas are 0.16 GiB, which is the ~84M-param VAE in 16-bit. The source and latent tensors are only megabytes.

This contradicts README.md:600-601 ("over the weights already loaded: nothing is downloaded and nothing more is held on the card"), docs/design-notes.md:398 and the commit message. Read strictly, those sentences are true only about duplicated weights: the sibling holds no second copy. They are not true of what is resident on the card during a pass.

It is stock diffusers img2img behaviour under that offload chain, not a logic error the commit introduced. The cost is about 0.16 GiB of peak (about 1.3% on FLUX), and the commit's own table already shows it. Severity stays low. Between the images of a batch, the VAE also stays resident through the next image's text encode, but that is below the denoise peak and adds nothing to it.

verdict.claim: `Img2ImgStub` is meant to make the progress test pin that the step callback reads the pipeline's own count (`_pipe.num_timesteps`, as `diffusers_backend.py:576` does) rather than computing `refine.steps_run`. The contract: CLAUDE.md's refine bullet and docs/design-notes.md:466-477 say the step callback reports the count the pipeline itself ran, read from `pipe.num_timesteps`, because the two pipeline families round differently. I checked the rounding in the installed diffusers source:

- FLUX img2img (`pipeline_flux_img2img.py:479-486`) uses `steps - int(steps - steps*strength)`.
- Both set `_num_timesteps = len(timesteps)` (`:1382`, `:943`).
So 28 steps at 0.4 runs 11 steps on SDXL and 12 on FLUX.1.

The code does what the docs say. `backend/backends/diffusers_backend.py:576` reads `getattr(_pipe, "num_timesteps", None) or total`. The defect is in the test, not the code.

`Img2ImgStub` (`tests/test_refine.py:465-487`) says it models the flow pipelines' count: `n - int(n*(1-strength))`. But every refine test that runs it uses a step/strength pair where that count equals the floor `refine.steps_run` (`backend/refine.py:142`, `max(1, int(steps*strength))`):
- 10 steps at 0.4: 4 either way (`:517`)
- 10 steps at 0.5: 5 either way (`:557`, `:566`)

So the progress assertion `progress == [(n, 8) for n in range(1, 9)]` at `:539`, with the comment at `:537` ("the steps the pipeline says it ran - four of ten here"), would pass just the same if the callback computed the floor. The cancel test at `:574` only counts callbacks, so it is the same either way. No other test reads `num_timesteps`; a grep of the repo outside `.venv` finds it only at `diffusers_backend.py:576`, the stub and the design note.

Nothing upstream guards this. `test_api_refine.py` runs on `FakeBackend`, not `DiffusersBackend`, so it never reaches this callback.

If the floor were swapped in, a real FLUX.1 pass at 28 steps and 0.4 runs 12 callbacks while the floor says 11. The bar would then end at 12/11 per image. The preview gate `step + 1 < steps` (`:580`) would also skip the second-to-last step's frame. Both are off by one. The current code is correct, so this is a gap in test coverage, rated low.

The README is wrong here, not the code. The code does this on purpose and a test covers it. Carrying the PNG's size is right when the PNG is itself a refined image: it reproduces the pass exactly. But it means the 1.5 default never applies under `--from-image`.

The path:
1. `_apply_image_settings` (generate.py:326-330) copies the PNG's `size` into `args.width`/`args.height` when no size flag was given.
2. In `main()`, `sized = any(... args.width, args.height ...)` is then True.
3. The branch `if args.refine is not None and (args.scale is not None or not sized)` is skipped, so `refine.scaled(..., DEFAULT_SCALE)` is never called and the request keeps the PNG's size.

No guard anywhere warns or refuses. The design notes do not cover how the CLI sizes a pass under `--from-image`, so nothing there justifies the README's wording.

verdict.finder_title: Docs say diffusers ships no image-to-image path for Anima; 0.40 does
verdict.claim: For Anima Turbo, the user-facing text gives a false reason for the missing Refine pass: docs/anime-model-guide.md:77-78, README.md:599-606 ("So it exists where diffusers has one" with Anima under "no") and the refine tooltip `_REFINE_HINTS[False]` at backend/model_defaults.py:886 all say diffusers has no image-to-image path. diffusers 0.40 does ship one for Anima: `AnimaImg2ImgVaeEncoderStep`, `AnimaImg2ImgCoreDenoiseStep`, and `AnimaAutoBlocks`/`AnimaModularPipeline` with an "img2img" workflow, over the same component types `AnimaTurboPipeline` uses. The statement is still true for NetaYume and NewBie. The refusal behaviour itself is correct; only the reason is wrong.
verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds, at least for Anima. I found nothing that refutes it.

**Where the commit says it:** commit 212f41c tells users in three places that Anima Turbo has no Refine pass because diffusers has no image-to-image path for it.
- docs/anime-model-guide.md:77-78 says "**Anima Turbo, NetaYume and NewBie** do not, because Diffusers ships no image-to-image pipeline for them".
- README.md:599-606 says "It runs the image-to-image pipeline diffusers ships beside the checkpoint's own ... So it exists where diffusers has one", then lists Anima Turbo under "no".
- backend/model_defaults.py:883-888 is `_REFINE_HINTS[False]`: "This checkpoint's pipeline has no image-to-image counterpart in diffusers". `hints_for` at :965-966 shows it on Anima, because the profile's `refine_supported` is False there (asserted in tests/test_refine.py:68).

**What diffusers 0.40 actually ships:**
- In diffusers/modular_pipelines/anima/modular_blocks_anima.py:
  - :129 defines `AnimaImg2ImgCoreDenoiseStep`. Its blocks run text conditioning, image input, `AnimaImg2ImgSetTimestepsStep`, `AnimaImg2ImgPrepareLatentsStep` and `AnimaDenoiseStep`.
  - :257-258 is `AnimaAutoCoreDenoiseStep`, with branches `["img2img","text2image"]`.
  - :312-373 is `AnimaAutoBlocks`, whose `_workflow_map` has `"img2img": {"image": True, "prompt": True}`.
- encoders.py:316 defines `AnimaImg2ImgVaeEncoderStep`.
- `AnimaAutoBlocks` and `AnimaModularPipeline` are exported from the top-level diffusers package.
- These blocks use the same component types `AnimaTurboPipeline` registers: `AnimaTextConditioner`, `CosmosTransformer3DModel`, `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler` and `AutoencoderKLQwenImage`.
- The app's wrapper (backend/backends/anima_pipeline.py:26) imports `AnimaCoreDenoiseStep` and `AnimaDecodeStep` from that same module. Its own docstring calls them "Diffusers' Anima text-to-image blocks".

So diffusers does ship an image-to-image path for Anima.

**Why the app has no pass, and why the code is fine:** the real reason is the integration, not the library. `refine.sibling` only recognises a diffusers-exported `<Name>Img2ImgPipeline` class. The local `AnimaTurboPipeline` has none, so `sibling` returns None (tests/test_refine.py:66). design-notes.md:412-413 says this correctly ("Anima and NewBie run this repo's own pipeline classes, which have no sibling"), and so does the refine.py module docstring ("neither do the local Anima and NewBie pipelines"). The behaviour itself is right: Anima is refused, the field is greyed, and the profile, describe and tests agree.

**What is wrong:** only the stated reason, and only in the user-facing text (guide, README table lead-in, tooltip). The design notes do not justify that claim; they give a different one. For NetaYume (Lumina 2) and NewBie the claim is true: there are no Lumina or NewBie image-to-image classes or modular blocks in 0.40. Krea 2, FLUX.2 and ERNIE modular blocks have no img2img either.

**Correction to location:** the "because Diffusers ships no image-to-image pipeline" clause starts on line 78, not 77. The same defect also appears at README.md:599-606 and backend/model_defaults.py:886.

**Severity:** low. Nothing behaves wrongly. A user or maintainer is told an upstream limitation exists when the limit is this app's integration.

verdict.finder_title: SDXL at 0.4 is put at flow sigma ~0.53; WAI's leading-spaced scheduler gives 0.50
verdict.claim: docs/design-notes.md:521-523 says SDXL at strength 0.4 starts at the SNR of a flow sigma of "about 0.53". All four SDXL checkpoints here (Animagine, Kohaku, Illustrious, WAI) use leading-spaced Euler or Euler Ancestral schedulers. At their profile's 28 steps, the pass starts at t=351, sigma_eps 0.990, which is flow sigma 0.498, about 0.50. 0.53 is what trailing spacing would give. The figure is inaccurate, but the notes' stated target is "about half noise" (line 532-533) and no code or profile value depends on 0.53. The reviewer's further claim, that the Qwen-Image row is tied to the same wrong SDXL target, is not supported.
verdict.reasoning:
The number is wrong, but the consequence is smaller than the reviewer says.

What the doc says: docs/design-notes.md:521-523, added in 212f41c, states "SDXL's epsilon schedule at 0.4 starts where the signal-to-noise ratio is that of a flow sigma of about 0.53."

What the code does:
- All four SDXL profiles run 28 steps at refine_strength 0.4: Animagine (backend/model_defaults.py:315/323), Kohaku (:349/357), Illustrious (:383/391) and WAI (:647/655).
- All four schedulers use timestep_spacing "leading" with steps_offset 1. Animagine and Kohaku use EulerDiscrete; the converted Illustrious and WAI trees use EulerAncestral.
- The refine pass passes no denoising_start. So diffusers' StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline.get_timesteps (.venv/.../pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py:647-657) takes the strength branch: init_timestep = int(28*0.4) = 11, t_start = 17, then set_begin_index(17). add_noise therefore uses sigmas[17].
- At that index t = 351 and sigma_eps = 0.990. Equal SNR means (1-s)/s = 1/sigma_eps, so s = sigma_eps/(1+sigma_eps) = 0.498.
- 0.53 comes from "trailing" spacing (t=392, 0.531) or from a naive t = 0.4*1000 (0.538). No SDXL checkpoint here uses either.
- Leading spacing never reaches 0.53 at any common step count: 0.48-0.52 over 15-50 steps.
- docs/verified.md records no SDXL starting sigma, so nothing measured backs 0.53.

Where the reviewer goes too far:
- The failure scenario is overstated. The design notes give the target as "about half noise" (line 532-533; README.md:590 says the same), not 0.53.
- The Qwen-Image row (line 542) reports Qwen's own dynamic-shift arithmetic. It is not tied to the SDXL figure.
- No code reads this number, and the SDXL default of 0.4 rests on WAI's author's range and the WAI measurement, not on this sigma.

So this is an inaccurate figure in the design notes, in a section that otherwise gives sigmas to two decimals. It does not change any behaviour.
verdict.reproduction:
Ran two scratch scripts with `uv run python`: verify_sdxl_refine_sigma.py and verify_sdxl_refine_sigma_steps.py, both in the scratchpad. Each imports backend.config before diffusers, loads the cached scheduler_config.json of WAI, Illustrious, Animagine 4.0 and Kohaku Zeta into the installed scheduler class, calls set_timesteps(28) and reads timesteps and sigmas at t_start = 28 - int(28*0.4) = 17.

Output, the same for all four checkpoints:
- leading (their actual config): t=351, sigma_eps=0.990, flow=0.498
- linspace: t=370, sigma_eps=1.055, flow=0.513
- trailing: t=392, sigma_eps=1.134, flow=0.531

Leading spacing at other step counts: 15 steps 0.481, 20 steps 0.498, 25 steps 0.506, 30 steps 0.508, 40 steps 0.518, 50 steps 0.522.

Raw timesteps: t=400 gives 0.538 and t=392 gives 0.531.

verdict.finder_title: After Unload the page drops the refine source: Reuse and Generate render directly
verdict.claim: The refine capability depends on the profile before a load. An unprofiled checkpoint (not in the catalogue) whose pipeline has an Img2Img sibling, such as an SDXL fine-tune given through LOCAL_DIFFUSION_MODEL_ID, gets `_FALLBACK`'s guess `refine_supported` False whenever nothing is loaded: at every server start and after Unload. Until a load, the page greys the Refine field and says the checkpoint has no pass. `reuse()` drops a refined record's source (gallery.js:377), and `collect()` drops a remembered one (generation.js:35). A Generate or grid then renders plain images at the refined size with no refusal. That bypasses the protection design-notes.md:496-500 gives as the reason for the submit refusal, and it contradicts the "model-agnostic" claim at design-notes.md:413-414. It affects only checkpoints outside the catalogue; catalogue profiles are held to diffusers by tests. The field is visibly greyed with a note, and loading the model first avoids it. Low severity.
verdict.reasoning:
The path exists as described, but only for a checkpoint outside the catalogue, so it is not the medium-severity defect claimed.

How it happens:
- `_FALLBACK` guesses `refine_supported: False` (backend/model_defaults.py:776).
- `describe()` gives None while nothing is loaded (backend/backends/diffusers_backend.py:798), so `_merged_defaults` falls back to that guess (backend/main.py:296-308).
- On every change, status.js:194-196 copies the merged value into `refineSupported`.
- Once `refineSupported` is false:
  - `reuse()` at gallery.js:377 sets `refineSource` to null for a refined record, after setting width and height to the refined size at gallery.js:371-372. It then calls `showError('')`.
  - `collect()` at generation.js:35 sends `refine: null`. Strength is undefined because `syncConditioning` disables `els.strength` (sizes.js:212-214).
  - `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:390ff) only acts when `request.refine` is not None, so nothing refuses the request. The job loads the model and renders a plain text-to-image at the refined size.
- The same happens without Reuse. `restorePanel` keeps a remembered source "whatever the checkpoint" (panel.js:74-81), and `collect()` still drops it. So after a restart, which always comes up unloaded, a Generate or a grid renders plain cells at the 1.5x size.
- design-notes.md:496-500 says the submit refusal exists to stop exactly this ("a night of new pictures"). The page gets around that refusal by never sending the source.

No guard upstream catches it. If the page did send the source, the server would refuse with the same false "has no refine pass" 422. The server and page agree with each other, and both are wrong before a load.

Why I downgrade it:
1. It needs an unprofiled id. Every catalogue entry has a profile whose guess `tests/test_refine.py` holds to the installed diffusers. CLAUDE.md makes a catalogue entry that reaches `_FALLBACK` a test failure. So the guess and the live answer agree for every catalogued checkpoint. Neither hassaku nor SDXL base appears anywhere in the repo's profiles or catalogue.
2. It is the documented guess-until-load design. design-notes.md:413-417 and 293 apply it to `reference_supported` too, and that pattern predates this commit (gallery.js:364, generation.js:29). The gating in `collect()` is itself written into CLAUDE.md.
3. The UI is not silent at Generate time. The Refine field is greyed with "(this checkpoint has no refine pass)" (sizes.js:282), and the size line stops saying "refining image N". The note is wrong for this checkpoint, but it is visible.
4. The record stays honest (`refine` is None), and the Load button gives the pass back.

What remains is a contradiction between docs and code: design-notes.md:413-414 calls the refine capability model-agnostic, but before a load it depends on the profile.

A related point beyond this finding: the CLI at backend/generate.py:481 refuses `--refine` by the profile guess alone, before any load. So the CLI can never refine an unprofiled SDXL checkpoint, even though its live pipeline has a sibling.
verdict.reproduction:
I ran `uv run python -c "import backend.config; from backend.model_defaults import defaults_for; from backend import refine; import diffusers; ..."`. It printed:
- `John6666/hassaku-xl-illustrious-v31-sdxl False True` (the `refine_supported` and `mu_supported` guesses)
- `stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0 False True`
- `refine.sibling(StableDiffusionXLPipeline)` = `StableDiffusionXLImg2ImgPipeline`

So the guess before a load is False and the live answer would be True. I traced the page side in the code (status.js:194-203, gallery.js:370-385, generation.js:35-36, sizes.js:206-216 and 279-284, panel.js:74-81) but did not run it in a browser.

refuted.title: steps_run's floor is one short of what flow pipelines run, at FLUX's own default
refuted.summary: The arithmetic is right, but the floor is a documented, deliberate approximation and the code does what the docs say. Its effect on the estimate survives as F11.
refuted.why:
The reviewer's arithmetic is right, but the behaviour is a documented, deliberate approximation, and the code does what the docs say.

What checks out:
- diffusers 0.40's flow img2img `get_timesteps` returns `n - int(max(n - n*strength, 0))`. That is in pipeline_flux_img2img.py:477-486, and the same method is in z_image and qwenimage. SDXL's (pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py:647-656) uses `int(n*strength)`.
- `refine.steps_run` (refine.py:142) is `max(1, int(steps*strength))`.
- At each profile's own default strength (`model_defaults.defaults_for`), the floor and the pipeline's count differ only for FLUX.1 Krea dev and FLUX.1 dev: 28 steps at 0.1 gives a floor of 2, and the pipeline runs 3. Z-Anime (40 at 0.15 -> 6/6), Z-Image Turbo (8 at 0.25 -> 2/2), Qwen-Image (50 at 0.3 -> 15/15) and schnell (4 at 0.5 -> 2/2) agree. The SDXL profiles use SDXL's own rounding.
- `storage.step_cost_ms` (storage.py:516-523) divides refine rows by `steps_run`. It mixes them with direct rows at the same size and checkpoint, and `grid.estimate_seconds` (grid.py:593) multiplies back by the same count.

Why it is not a defect:
1. The contract chooses the floor knowingly. design-notes.md:466-477 states both roundings, with the example "28 steps at 0.4 is 11 on SDXL and 12 on FLUX.1". It says `step_cost_ms` divides by "`refine.steps_run` (the floor, at least one)" and that `estimate_seconds` "multiplies back by the same count". CLAUDE.md says "about `steps * strength` run (`refine.steps_run`, the floor; the step callback reports the pipeline's own count)". The `steps_run` docstring (refine.py:133-141) calls it "About how many", says the flow pipelines round differently, and says it is the floor "for the estimate and the progress bar's first frame". The progress events use `pipe.num_timesteps` (diffusers_backend.py:576), as documented.
2. The goal the note states for the division is that refining "does not price a direct render at a third of its cost". The floor avoids that under-pricing, so the goal is met.
3. A refine estimated from refine rows at the same strength is exact, because the same floor is in the numerator and the denominator. The scratch run below gives 16.9 s, the measured time.
4. What remains is a refine row pricing a direct render, or a refine at another strength. That is an advisory figure, and the design already accepts a larger error there: the per-call text encode, VAE encode and VAE decode. Even with the pipeline's exact count of 3, a direct 28-step 1536x1536 render would be estimated at 157.7 s against the 101.3 s measured. The floor moves that to 236.6 s.

The effect is real but limited to a stated approximation inside an estimate that is already approximate. No row, reproduction key, refusal or progress event is wrong. Nothing upstream guards it, but nothing needs to.

refuted.title: Merge turns a refine whose source is gone into a direct-render record
refuted.summary: The commit's documented and tested choice: a merge drops a source that did not come across, with its strength, and counts it unresolved.
refuted.why:
The mechanics the reviewer describes are accurate, but the behaviour is the commit's deliberate, documented and tested choice. The code does exactly what the contract says, so under the review rules it is not a defect.

Code path:
- At reindex.py:298-304, a source id that is not in id_map becomes None and is counted in `unresolved_references`.
- At reindex.py:225 and :340, the strength is nulled along with the source.
- `_copy_in` writes that metadata into the copied PNG.
- In B, `storage.completed_cells` (storage.py:694, `refine_key(None, None)`) and `step_cost_ms` (storage.py:515-521, `refine is not None` gate) then treat the row as a direct render.

Contract:
- docs/design-notes.md:508-509 says "a database merge remaps the source id with the reference ids and drops one whose image did not come across".
- CLAUDE.md:351 says "a database merge remaps the source id as it does a reference's".
- The reference policy this extends is justified at design-notes.md:1098-1100: "a missing or conflicting predecessor is dropped and counted rather than left pointing at an unrelated destination row".
- tests/test_refine.py:425-430 asserts the drop for both the row and the copied PNG chunk ("Dropped with its strength rather than left naming an unrelated image", "should this gallery be rebuilt from files").
- The merge reports the drop: reindex.py:476-478 prints "N unresolved reference(s)", and the README says unresolved references are reported.

The same trade-off already applied before this commit. A klein row whose reference was dropped also becomes a no-reference record in CellKey, the resume key and Reuse. The commit applied the documented policy unchanged.

Alternatives within the schema:
- Keeping the source's id would name an unrelated row in B, which is the hazard the docs reject.
- A strength with no source is not a setting (`applied()`).

So there is no representation the code fails to use. No upstream guard stops the scenario (no delete path protects a refine source; clear.py and storage have no such check), so the drop is reachable. Its effects are edge cases:
- (a) The resume or Re-render match needs a direct render of the same prompt, seed, steps and CFG at exactly the refined size.
- (b) The step cost is a median of up to 20 rows at that exact size, so it is an estimate only.
- (c) In A, Reuse also drops a gone source with a note and renders a plain image.

These are consequences of the documented design choice, not code that contradicts it.

refuted.title: CLI refuses refine on unprofiled checkpoints with a sibling, with a false message
refuted.summary: The design notes say the CLI decides before its load, from the profile; the CLI has no other answer at that point.
refuted.why:
The facts are right, but they describe the documented design, not a defect.

1. The design notes for the refine pass say the CLI refuses before its load, from the profile. They say a source is "refused at submit (`_refuse_unusable_inputs`, and the CLI before its load) where the checkpoint has no pass". They also say "Each profile carries `refine_supported` as its guess before a load, `describe()` answers from the class after it". CLAUDE.md says the same: "`refine_supported` is profiled before a load ... unsupported ... is refused at submit and by the CLI". The CLI decides everything before it loads. That covers the resume prune (generate.py:704) and the duplicate count (generate.py:835), both through `backend.applied()`, which uses the profile when nothing is loaded (diffusers_backend.py:301-313). So the profile's guess is the only answer the CLI has at generate.py:481.

2. This copies the CLI's existing reference check exactly: `if references and not profile["reference_supported"]` (generate.py:646). An unprofiled id whose pipeline takes `image` is refused there in the same way.

3. The server gives the same answer in the same state. Before a load, `describe()` returns `refine_supported: None` (diffusers_backend.py:798), so `_merged_defaults` keeps the fallback's False (main.py:298-308). `_refuse_unusable_inputs` (main.py:402-410) then returns 422 with the same wording. Only after a load does either side have the class's answer, and the CLI never has a loaded pipeline when it decides.

4. Out-of-catalogue ids are not promised these features. CLAUDE.md's "any of them runs unchanged" means the catalogue entries, and "a catalogue entry that reaches the fallback is a test failure" (tests/test_profiles.py:375). Every catalogue checkpoint with a sibling is profiled True, and tests/test_refine.py checks each guess against the installed diffusers. The fallback is a generic guess and is wrong for SDXL base in other ways too, such as `mu_supported: True`.

5. `schemas.default_strength`'s comment ("a checkpoint the table does not know, whose pipeline turned out to have a pass") is reachable on the server after a load. It makes no claim about the CLI.

What remains is wording. "diffusers ships no image-to-image pipeline beside its own ... SDXL checkpoints have one" reads oddly for an off-catalogue SDXL id. The server shows the same text before a load, and it is not a behaviour defect.

refuted.title: Sibling release is tested on unload() only; the server calls try_unload()
refuted.summary: `try_unload` clears `_refine_pipe` too (diffusers_backend.py:261), and the test claims only what it checks.
refuted.why:
The facts are right, but they do not add up to a defect. The code does what the contract asks. `DiffusersBackend.try_unload` (backend/backends/diffusers_backend.py:256-266) takes the lock without blocking, then clears `_pipe`, `_call_params`, `_lora` and also `_refine_pipe` and `_refine_params` (line 261) before `_release()`. `unload()` does the same at line 245. The server's callers, main.py:181 (lifespan) and main.py:498 (Unload route), therefore release the sibling. The documented contract ("let go on unload", CLAUDE.md; design-notes.md:433-434, "dropped on unload") holds on both paths.

The test is not mislabelled either. Its comment at test_refine.py:548 says the sibling "has to go when the pipeline goes", and the test checks exactly that through `unload()`. Nowhere in CLAUDE.md, the design notes or the test claims that the server path is covered. The reviewer's failure scenario only applies if someone later deletes line 261. That is a request for one more regression test, not a current wrong behaviour, a broken invariant or a test that checks less than it says. The review brief excludes 'consider adding' items that have no concrete failure.

The gap is also not new to this commit. The `_lora = None` clearing in `try_unload` (line 260) was never tested against DiffusersBackend before it either. `grep try_unload tests/` finds only the FakeBackend wrappers in test_api_analysis.py.

refuted.title: CLI never re-checks the refine pass after backend.load(); rows silently plain
refuted.summary: Called the documented structure (refused before the load, dropped by `applied()` after), with a check after the load as hardening. F5's verifier confirmed the server's half of the same path; see F5.
refuted.why:
The code path the reviewer describes is real, but it is the behaviour the design documents and justifies, and it only opens for an id outside the catalogue.

1. The documented contract chooses exactly this structure. docs/design-notes.md:495-503 says the source is "refused at submit (`_refuse_unusable_inputs`, and the CLI before its load) where the checkpoint has no pass ... and dropped by `applied()` where it gets past that". The CLI does exactly that:
   - generate.py:481 checks `defaults_for(...)["refine_supported"]` before the load.
   - generate.py:927 is `backend.load()`.
   - diffusers_backend.py:541 has `generate()` call `applied()`, which uses `_refine_supported()` at diffusers_backend.py:321 once loaded.
   - generate.py:1018 saves `ran = backend.applied(cell.request)`.
   So the code does what the notes say.

2. The server has the same structure, so the CLI is not out of step with it. main.py:391-414 `_refuse_unusable_inputs` reads `_merged_defaults(backend.describe())` (main.py:288-310), which is still the profile guess while unloaded. Its docstring (main.py:395-400) says `applied()` keeps the record honest and the submit check is what stops the plain render. A page job submitted to an unloaded Kontext server takes the same route as the CLI run. CLAUDE.md likewise says `refine_supported` "is profiled before a load, each guess held to the installed diffusers, and the class's answer after it".

3. Within the catalogue the guess cannot be wrong. tests/test_refine.py:47-57 parametrizes over test_profiles.CASES (tests/test_profiles.py:27-44, every catalogue checkpoint and its real class).    - FLUX.1-Fill-dev / FluxFillPipeline
   - Qwen-Image-Edit / QwenImageEditPipeline
   - Qwen-Image-Edit-2509 / QwenImageEditPlusPipeline

   These are image-editing pipelines the catalogue does not list. The launch menu labels such an id "unrecognised id" (launch.py:419-421), and its profile is the family's by token match. The same token mismatch already misguesses `reference_supported` for Kontext: the flux profile says False, but the live class has `image`.

The resume, the duplicate count and `run_id` all read `applied()`. The scenario also overstates one detail: FluxKontextPipeline rescales any requested size to `max_area` 1024**2 (pipeline_flux_kontext.py:841-848), so it would not render at 1536x1536.
