refuted.title: After Unload, refinements this checkpoint made are refused with a false 422
refuted.summary: Documented: `refine_supported` is profiled before a load. The page's side survives as P1.
refuted.why:
The mechanics are as described, but the behaviour is the documented design, not a defect. Unloaded, DiffusersBackend.describe() reports refine_supported None (diffusers_backend.py:798). _merged_defaults (main.py:298-308) then keeps the profile's guess, and an id the table does not know gets _FALLBACK with refine_supported False (model_defaults.py:776, _profile_for at 798-805). _refuse_unusable_inputs (main.py:402-410) refuses on that guess, and /api/rerender reaches the same check (main.py:1120-1124).

The contract chooses this on purpose:
- CLAUDE.md: "`refine_supported` is profiled before a load ... and the class's answer after it; unsupported ... is refused at submit and by the CLI".
- design-notes.md:414-417: "Each profile carries `refine_supported` as its guess before a load, `describe()` answers from the class after it, `/api/status` merges the two like `reference_supported`".
- design-notes.md:549-550 expects an unknown checkpoint to run a pass only once its class answers: "A checkpoint the table does not know ... runs at `refine.DEFAULT_STRENGTH`".
- tests/test_refine.py:70-71 asserts the exact behaviour reported: "An unrecognised checkpoint is not promised one either, until it loads" (`assert not defaults_for("nobody/whatever")["refine_supported"]`).

reference_supported, mu_supported and the other capabilities follow the same guess-until-load pattern. The page agrees with the server: status shows False while unloaded, so the Refine field is greyed with the same explanation until Load. Refusing a capability the profile cannot vouch for, rather than accepting it, is the intended direction. If the server accepted the request, applied() before load would drop the source anyway (diffusers_backend.py:301-313).

The suggestion that rerender should trust rows pinned to settings.model_id would be a new inference, not something the contract requires. "Re-render ... carry both" holds: the cells carry refine and strength (main.py:1106-1107), and the capability check refuses them.

The only true inaccuracy is wording. For an unknown SDXL id before a load, the 422 text "diffusers ships no image-to-image pipeline beside its own" (main.py:407-409), and the matching _REFINE_HINTS[False] tooltip, state a guess as fact. That is a misleading message, not wrong behaviour or a broken invariant. The CLI's refusal at generate.py:481 was reported separately, and there it can never be overcome because the CLI checks before it loads. On the server, pressing Load is the documented path to the live answer.

refuted.title: Check and the critic refused over the refine steps/strength pair they never read
refuted.summary: Check takes the body Generate would send, and a body Generate refuses has always been refused by Check.
refuted.why:
The mechanism is real, but it is not a defect. It follows the documented contract, and the parts of the claim that would make it one do not hold.

1. The mechanism. PromptAnalysisRequest (schemas.py:272) subclasses GenerateRequest, so it inherits _refine_leaves_a_step (schemas.py:119-131). collect() (web/generation.js:35-36) sends `refine` and `strength`. Both checkPrompt (analysis.js:79) and askCritic (analysis.js:629) POST that body, so Krea dev with a source, Steps 8 and Strength 0.1 gets a 422.

2. This is the documented design. Check takes "the body Generate would send (`PromptAnalysisRequest`)" (design-notes.md:2435-2436; CLAUDE.md "Three layers over the body Generate sends"). The schema docstring says "The whole request rather than the text alone" (schemas.py:273-279). A body Generate refuses has always been refused by Check, including on fields the analyser never reads. A grep finds no request.width/steps/seed/num_images reads in prompt_rules, prompt_encoding or critic. Yet width=1000 typed into the W box (min 256, max 3168, so in range) already gave a 422 from Check before this commit, through _multiple_of_16. So the claim that "before this commit, no in-range panel state could make Check 422 on a non-prompt field" is wrong. The new validator adds one more Generate-invalid body to an existing class.

3. The refusal is accurate, not wrong. refuted.title: Deleted refine source refused as 'no gallery image with id N', source unnamed
refuted.summary: The message is true, names the id and predates the commit; the commit fixed the one branch that misnamed the kind of image.
refuted.why:
The code does what the reviewer says: in storage.py:1080-1084 the unknown-id branch raises "no gallery image with id N" without using `noun`, and main.py:411-414 passes that text through as a 422. That is not a defect, for these reasons:

1. The message is true and it names the id. It never calls the source by the wrong name. Before the commit (`git show 212f41c^:backend/storage.py`, lines 1035-1045), the unknown branch already said "no gallery image with id N" and named no kind of image. Only the missing-file branch hard-coded "the file for reference image N", which would be wrong for a refine source. The commit added `noun` to fix exactly that branch (storage.py:1087-1089). So the source is "resolved under its own noun": every message that names a kind of image names the source's own kind. The docstring (storage.py:1068-1069) and design-notes.md:496 are both satisfied.

2. The message is the contract that is actually tested. tests/test_api_refine.py:53-58 (`test_an_unknown_source_is_named`) asserts "no gallery image with id 4242" for an unknown refine source, and test_api_refine.py:149-155 asserts the same text for a source deleted before a Re-render. tests/test_refine.py:152 pins it at the storage layer too. "Named" in these tests means the id is named. Both tests pass.

3. The message cannot be ambiguous. _refuse_unusable_inputs checks refine (main.py:402-414) before references (main.py:415-427). In model_defaults.py no profile has both `reference_supported` and `refine_supported` true: klein has references and no pass, and the pass checkpoints have no references. So a refusal naming an id cannot be confused with a reference image.

4. The page shows the same number. The Refine field's note reads "(image N, WxH)" (sizes.js:286), the chip's button is labelled "Remove refine source image N" (sizes.js:297-298), and the size line says "refining image N" (sizes.js:114-117). These all sit in the same panel the comparison reads its request from, so the "image 4" in the error points to something on the page.

5. Seeing a deletion made in another tab mid-session is outside the documented design. design-notes.md:511-513 says the page asks GET /api/images/{id} only for a source restored from localStorage or carried in by Reuse (loadRefineSource, sizes.js:360-380). forgetImages (gallery.js:244-249) covers deletions made on this page. smoke-refine.json:109-115 covers exactly those two cases. A source deleted in another tab is left for the server to refuse, and it is refused before anything renders. The run is not done as plain text-to-image, which is the real invariant (main.py:395-400).

What remains is a wish for a more specific error wording. No behaviour is wrong and no documented invariant is broken.

gaps.why: docs/verified.md and the README's refine table rest on GPU runs whose evidence is on disk at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\local-diffusion-refine-validation (validate_refine.py, sweep_refine.py, plus per-checkpoint validation.log, results.json, sweep JSONs, a database and output PNGs). The docs reviewer said these claims are 'only the GPU can reproduce' and did not open the evidence, and no other reviewer did either. The recorded progress tuples are also the only real data on how many steps a pass actually runs compared with refine.steps_run's floor. That question decided one REFUTED finding and one CONFIRMED finding (step_cost_ms / estimate).

Every reviewer reasoned about the real diffusers img2img siblings from source only. The core reviewer believed no tokenizers were cached offline. In fact the FLUX.1-Krea-dev, SDXL-base and Z-Anime tokenizers are in the HF cache and the RTX 5080 is idle, so a tiny real pipeline can run generate()'s refine branch. The card validation (verified.md) covered only fp8 with model offload. Not executed anywhere: offload 'none'/'sequential', true CFG with a negative prompt through FluxImg2ImgPipeline, and Mu on Z-Image/Z-Anime through schedule.shifted_sigmas with a strength slice. The interactions reviewer listed sequential offload as 'reasoned only, never executed'.

The submit refusal (main._refuse_unusable_inputs via _merged_defaults) and the CLI gate (backend/generate.py ~481 and ~633) decide refine support from model_defaults' family-token guess whenever no pipeline is loaded. After the load, DiffusersBackend.applied() decides from the live class and silently drops the source if refine.sibling finds none. That would render and record a plain text-to-image at the enlarged size, which is the outcome the refusal exists to prevent. The reverse case (guess False, live True) greys the page and 422s until a load. Reviewers only noted that test_refine's CASES table is hand-maintained. Nobody traced the before-load path end to end, or what each cached checkpoint's real model_index class resolves to.

web/analysis.js has no refine handling. Yet checkPrompt and the critic post collect(), which now carries `refine` and `strength`, and PromptAnalysisRequest inherits GenerateRequest's new _refine_leaves_a_step validator and default_strength fill. comparePayload spreads gridPayload(), so a prompt comparison silently becomes a refine pass of whatever source is in the panel. Reviewers found only the strength_axis multiplication. The web reviewer judged Check carrying refine fields 'consistent' without exercising it. Nobody checked the stale rule, Check/critique refusals, or what a comparison under a source actually renders and reports.
